articles.title: British Business Bank: Additional £40 Million Commitment Supports Harwood Fund
articles.snippet:
The British Business Bank has committed an additional £40 million to Harwood Private Capital to increase the availability of flexible financing for smaller and lower-middle-market businesses across the United Kingdom.
The post British Business Bank: Additional £40 Million Commitment Supports Harwood Fund appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
British Business Bank: Additional £40 Million Commitment Supports Harwood Fund
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:09 PM
British Business Bank: Additional £40 Million Commitment Supports Harwood Fund
The British Business Bank has committed an additional £40 million to Harwood Private Capital to increase the availability of flexible financing for smaller and lower-middle-market businesses across the United Kingdom.
The investment supports the first closing of Harwood Private Capital UK Fund II. Commitments to the fund and its related co-investment vehicles now total approximately £120 million.
Harwood will use the capital to provide debt financing for privately held companies pursuing organic expansion, acquisitions, and shareholder transitions. The strategy gives business owners an alternative to conventional bank lending or a complete sale through an M&A transaction.
The commitment increases the British Business Bank’s total investment with Harwood to £75 million. The government-owned development bank previously committed £35 million to the manager’s inaugural HPC UK SME Fund in 2020.
Harwood specializes in flexible private-credit solutions for lower-middle-market companies. Its target borrowers include founder- and family-owned businesses that need additional growth capital but want to preserve ownership and strategic control.
The inaugural fund invested across digital technology, clean-energy supply chains, manufacturing, tourism, and other sectors. One portfolio example is Western Marinas, a Welsh marina operator that used Harwood financing to restore facilities in Wales and southwest England.
That investment supported local jobs and family-operated businesses while attracting visitors and economic activity to surrounding coastal communities. It demonstrates how private credit can finance physical assets and regional companies that may not fit the standardized requirements of traditional lenders.
The British Business Bank’s mandate is to improve access to capital for smaller companies and address financing gaps that can limit growth, productivity, and job creation. In its 2025-2026 financial year, the bank supported £9.4 billion of financing for approximately 38,000 businesses.
That total included £1.3 billion of public funding, £4.3 billion of private capital attracted through the bank’s programs, and £3.7 billion of guaranteed lending. Around 30,000 recipients had not previously received support through the institution.
Harwood Private Capital UK Fund II is intended to extend this impact by supplying customized debt structures for companies whose requirements may not be served adequately by banks or private equity investors.
KEY QUOTES:
“Many smaller businesses continue to face challenges accessing the flexible growth capital they need to scale, invest and realise their ambitions. Harwood has developed a strong track record of providing tailored financing solutions to UK SMEs, particularly those that have not been backed by private equity. Our commitment will help increase the availability of growth capital for businesses, support economic growth and create jobs throughout the UK.”
Adam Kelly, Managing Director of Debt and Regional Funds at the British Business Bank

News provided by
Promise Robotics

Round led by White Star Capital follows a multi-year agreement with America's largest homebuilder and the launch of Promise's first U.S. facility in Phoenix.
PHOENIX , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Promise Robotics , the company bringing Physical AI to homebuilding, today announced the close of a $40 million CAD Series B funding round led by White Star Capital to expand the production infrastructure needed to scale homebuilding. The round also included participation from Horizons Ventures, Radical Ventures, Public Sector Pension Investment Board (PSP Investments).
Homebuilders are under increasing pressure to expand housing production, but scaling through traditional construction methods alone is constrained by skilled labor availability and the complexity of adding production capacity market by market. Promise Robotics addresses that constraint by giving builders access to automated production capacity without requiring them to develop and operate factories themselves. The funding round will support the continued expansion of that production network across North America.
This announcement comes just weeks after Promise Robotics expanded its U.S. production network and signed a multi-year commercial agreement with D.R. Horton, America's largest homebuilder by volume. As the first major U.S. homebuilder to leverage Promise Robotics' Factory-as-a-Service® (FaaS) platform, D.R. Horton's adoption underscores growing demand for scalable, technology-driven homebuilding solutions. With production already live in Calgary and Nisku, Canada, more than 2,500 housing units under contract across three markets, and its first U.S. facility planned for Phoenix, the company is demonstrating the momentum and operating scale this new investment will help accelerate.
FaaS gives a broad range of homebuilders across geographies access to an integrated production platform that takes existing home designs and translates them into a coordinated production process spanning robotic manufacturing, factory operations, and onsite installation. Through FaaS, builders can access automated production capacity without developing and operating their own factories, helping them improve cycle times, increase capacity, and scale more predictably across communities and markets.
"Homebuilding can't scale on trade labor alone, and builders shouldn't have to become manufacturers to grow. We're building the production infrastructure the industry can scale on; a network of intelligent factories that get better with every home it helps build. This round lets us extend that network across North America," said Ramtin Attar, CEO and co-founder of Promise Robotics.

articles.title: Star Holdings: Q3 Revenue Reaches $39.9 Million As Net Loss Widens To $45.1 Million
articles.snippet:
Star Holdings reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $39.9 million, up from $28.1 million a year earlier, as land development activity increased. The real estate-focused company nevertheless recorded a net loss of $45.1 million, compared with net income of $274,000 in the third quarter of 2025.
The post Star Holdings: Q3 Revenue Reaches $39.9 Million As Net Loss Widens To $45.1 Million appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Star Holdings: Q3 Revenue Reaches $39.9 Million As Net Loss Widens To $45.1 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:50 AM
Star Holdings: Q3 Revenue Reaches $39.9 Million As Net Loss Widens To $45.1 Million
Star Holdings reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $39.9 million, up from $28.1 million a year earlier, as land development activity increased. The real estate-focused company nevertheless recorded a net loss of $45.1 million, compared with net income of $274,000 in the third quarter of 2025.
Operating lease income was $1.7 million, compared with $1.8 million a year earlier. Interest income and other operating sources contributed to the quarter, while land development revenue increased to $21 million from $1.7 million. The company recognized revenue from the sale of a land parcel during the period, with related development cost of sales reducing the transaction’s contribution.
The loss allocable to common shareholders was $45.1 million, or $3.74 per share, compared with income allocable to common shareholders of $1.8 million, or $0.14 per share, in the prior-year quarter. Results reflected the timing of property transactions, carrying costs, interest expense, and changes in the value or performance of Star’s remaining assets and investments.
For the first nine months of 2026, total revenue was $80.2 million, compared with $84.8 million a year earlier. The nine-month net loss narrowed to $18.1 million from $47.5 million, while the loss allocable to common shareholders improved to $13.9 million from $45.1 million.
Star Holdings was created to hold and realize value from a portfolio of legacy real estate assets and other investments. Its results can vary significantly between periods because land sales, loan repayments, hotel activity, and asset dispositions do not occur on a uniform schedule. Third-quarter revenue growth therefore showed progress in monetizing property, but the substantial reported loss demonstrated the continuing costs and valuation effects associated with managing the portfolio. Future performance will depend heavily on the timing and economics of additional asset sales, development activity, and resolution of remaining obligations.

articles.title: JPYC Raises $38M in Extended Series B To Grow Yen Stablecoin Adoption
articles.snippet: JPYC Raises $38M in Extended Series B To Grow Yen Stablecoin Adoption CoinMarketCap
articles.text:
Japan's registered yen stablecoin issuer JPYC Inc has secured a total of 6 billion yen ($38 million) in an extended Series B funding round, drawing in a major domestic logistics firm as it moves to expand its footprint in the country's growing digital payments market.
The latest injection came from AZ-COM Maruwa, a Tokyo-listed logistics company, which committed 1 billion yen ($6.3 million) to the round. Earlier in the Series B, Metaplanet Ventures had invested 400 million yen ($2.53 million) in March.
Logistics Firm Plans Stablecoin Payroll Use
AZ-COM Maruwa, which counts Amazon Japan among its clients, said it plans to use JPYC to pay fees and salaries to roughly 2,300 business partners and individual contractors. The company reportedly sees the speed of yen-denominated stablecoin transfers as a practical solution for attracting business partners and managing driver shortages brought on by an aging workforce and stricter overtime rules. Nikkei reported the firm's plans last month.
JPYC said the round's proceeds will fund expansion of its financial and Web3 ecosystem and accelerate adoption of its yen-pegged stablecoin. The company launched last October as Japan's first registered stablecoin under the country's updated payment services rules, and has since begun piloting payments at a location of Lawson, Japan's third-largest convenience store chain.
Related Article: JPYC Stablecoin Set for 1st Large-Scale Corporate Use in Japan Logistics Deal
Traditional Banks Join Japan's Stablecoin Race
Japanese authorities have signaled support for broader stablecoin adoption, and established financial institutions have responded. SBI Group launched JPYSC in June as the country’s first trust bank-backed yen stablecoin. Three of Japan's largest banks, MUFG, SMBC, and Mizuho, are working together on a jointly issued stablecoin of their own.
AZ-COM Maruwa's investment stands out as a sign that industrial companies outside the financial sector are beginning to see yen stablecoins as practical infrastructure for supply chain payments and contractor settlement, rather than purely as a bet on digital assets.

articles.title: Graphon Labs Raises $35M Series A to Give AI Agents Long-Term Memory
articles.snippet: Graphon Labs Raises $35M Series A to Give AI Agents Long-Term Memory Wowtale
articles.text:
AI models keep getting smarter, yet they still struggle to understand the videos, documents and conversations people have accumulated. A startup building memory infrastructure that preserves the structure of that data has now raised a Series A.
Graphon Labs announced a $35 million Series A on Nov. 10. RRE Ventures led the round, and according to the press release, HP, Energy Impact Partners, Hitachi Ventures and Gaia VC participated. It comes six months after the company’s seed round and brings total funding to $43.3 million. Graphon plans to use the money to expand its infrastructure for developers and enterprise customers, then extend from the cloud and on-premises deployments to consumer devices.
The seed round drew some attention in Korea. According to May reports from The Next Web and SiliconAngle, Novera Ventures led the $8.3 million seed, with Perplexity Fund, Hitachi Ventures, Gaia Ventures, Samsung Next and GS Futures also participating. The Next Web reported that GS Group is an early customer, using the technology for convenience-store traffic analysis and safety monitoring on construction sites.
The problem Graphon targets is that AI “memory” today is mostly storage. Fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) have been used to bring company knowledge into models, but when documents are cut into pieces and searched as vectors, sentences with nearly identical words and opposite meanings, such as “refund allowed” and “refund not allowed,” can land close together. A rule may be found while the fragment holding its exception is missed. The company likens it to tearing a book apart page by page, crumpling the pages and trying to find them again.
Its answer is to keep the structure. Graphon reads mixed data such as video, images, spreadsheets, recordings and markdown files and builds a detailed graph without deciding in advance which relationships will matter. It then uses a compressed representation of that graph, the “graphon,” to guide where to search. According to press reports, the graphon is a mathematical concept formalized around 2008 by UC Berkeley professors Jennifer Chayes and Christian Borgs, among others, and the two serve as technical advisers.
Developers use it much like S3: put files in a bucket and Graphon builds the structure. The website lists four APIs, Storage, Search, Answer and Research. Products are split into Graphon Enterprise, Graphon Developer and Graphon On-Device Memory for phones, laptops, cameras and wearables, and enterprise customers can choose hosted, customer-managed VPC or on-premises deployment.
The performance figures are the company’s own. Graphon says it scored 93.9% accuracy on the LoCoMo conversational memory benchmark while using 58% fewer tokens than loading the full conversation, and 90.2% accuracy with 95% token savings on ConvoMem. On ATM-Bench, which spans video, audio and text, it reported 81.7%, 5.0 percentage points ahead of the next entry on the public leaderboard. None of these numbers has been independently verified.
Disclosed customers include the San Francisco 49ers and Hitachi Rail. The 49ers are weighing it for finding sponsorship opportunities and supporting staff work, while Hitachi Rail is evaluating its potential to surface contextual knowledge in industrial settings and improve AI reasoning. RRE Ventures’ Raju Rishi pointed to the fact that models can reason and agents can act, yet neither improves without accumulating knowledge, as the reason for investing.

articles.text:
Coframe: $35 Million Funding To Expand Autonomous AI Website And Advertising Optimization Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 3:28 PM
Coframe: $35 Million Funding To Expand Autonomous AI Website And Advertising Optimization Platform
Coframe, an artificial intelligence company developing self-optimizing digital experiences, has raised $35 million in total funding, including a $25 million Series A round co-led by Khosla Ventures and Hanabi Capital. The investment will support development of the company’s autonomous AI platform, which continuously generates, tests, and improves websites, landing pages, and advertising campaigns. The financing also included participation from executives and technology leaders associated with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind.
Coframe is developing what founder and CEO Josh Payne describes as the “living internet,” a model in which websites and other digital interfaces adapt continuously based on user interactions and business objectives.
Traditional websites generally display predetermined content and require development teams to make changes through scheduled design, engineering, and marketing projects.
Coframe’s platform is designed to automate much of that process by generating new content and design variations, testing their performance, and deploying improvements.
The company uses a specialized transformer model trained on user behavior alongside a team of AI agents responsible for different aspects of the optimization process.
Those agents perform functions resembling a strategist, designer, software engineer, quality assurance specialist, and data scientist.
Together, they can generate and evaluate hundreds of website or advertising variations within minutes.
The technology analyzes how visitors interact with digital experiences and uses those results to improve future versions.
Coframe says the platform can personalize content for different visitors while continuously adjusting interfaces to support conversion and engagement objectives.
The company reports that its technology has generated more than $300 million in incremental revenue for customers.
Its customer base includes Dropbox, Boston Consulting Group, Block, Backcountry, Sur La Table, and other businesses.
According to Coframe, customers have experienced conversion rate increases of 158% at Dropbox, 410% at Replit, and 60% at Cash App.
The company also reported that a Fortune 500 customer achieved a 70% increase in conversion within 30 days of signing its contract.
Across its customer base, Coframe says conversion rates have improved by more than 20% on average.
These performance figures are company-reported results and may vary across different implementations and customer environments.
At Dropbox, Coframe said an experiment that previously required approximately four weeks of engineering, design, and quality assurance work was created and deployed in 30 minutes.
The platform has also reported a 39% experiment success rate across thousands of tested variations.
Coframe says this represents more than three times the industry average, while customers have increased their experimentation frequency by tenfold or more.
Beyond website and advertising optimization, Coframe is developing capabilities for applications, email, and other digital experiences.
The company is also preparing for an internet in which AI agents increasingly perform research, product comparisons, and purchases on behalf of users.

articles.text:
Connie Health: $35 Million Credit Facility From Rivonia Road Capital Expandable To $100 Million For Medicare Brokerage Growth
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 4:57 PM
Connie Health: $35 Million Credit Facility From Rivonia Road Capital Expandable To $100 Million For Medicare Brokerage Growth
Connie Health, a technology-enabled Medicare insurance brokerage, has secured a $35 million asset-backed revolving credit facility from Rivonia Road Capital, with the potential to expand the financing commitment to $100 million. The facility will support the Boston-based company’s national expansion through organic growth and acquisitions as it increases the reach of its AI-powered insurance distribution platform.
The financing is backed by Connie Health’s existing Medicare insurance book of business and is designed to provide scalable capital for expanding its network of licensed insurance agents.
Connie plans to use the facility to support the origination of new insurance policies and strategic acquisitions of businesses that complement its existing operations.
The arrangement represents an additional source of financing beyond the approximately $85 million in equity capital Connie has raised since its founding.
The company’s most recent equity financing was a Series B round completed in early 2025 and led by HealthQuest Capital, with participation from Khosla Ventures, aMoon, and Pitango.
Expanding A Technology-Enabled Medicare Brokerage
Founded in 2019 by Oded Eran, David Luna, and Michael Scopa, Connie Health operates an insurance brokerage focused on helping Medicare beneficiaries evaluate and enroll in appropriate coverage.
The company’s offerings include Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement, and Medicare Prescription Drug Plans.
Connie combines a network of hundreds of local licensed insurance agents with a centralized technology platform designed to manage insurance distribution and customer service operations.
Under its operating model, customers are connected with a dedicated local agent who can help explain available coverage options, assist with enrollment, and provide support after a policy becomes effective.
The company believes maintaining these personal relationships can help beneficiaries navigate the complexity of Medicare coverage.
Its technology platform supports agents by automating and centralizing administrative activities.
These include lead generation, compliance management, back-office operations, and post-enrollment servicing.
By handling these functions through a common technology infrastructure, Connie aims to allow agents to spend more time assisting customers.
The platform incorporates AI capabilities intended to improve efficiency across insurance distribution and servicing.
The combination of local agent relationships and centralized technology is central to Connie’s growth strategy.
Using Asset-Backed Financing To Support Expansion
The $35 million facility provides Connie with access to revolving capital supported by its existing Medicare business.
Asset-backed revolving credit facilities allow eligible companies to borrow against specified assets or contractual cash flows, subject to applicable financing terms.
For insurance distribution businesses, existing policy portfolios and associated economic interests can provide a basis for structured lending arrangements.
Connie plans to use the facility to support the acquisition of new customers and expand its business through acquisitions.
